# External ODRL test suites

Other evaluators' test cases, vendored **unmodified** so that every translated corpus case is reproducible from source and every divergence can be checked against the original. Collected 2026-10-11; OVAL refreshed 2026-10-16, and twice on 2026-10-20.

| Directory | Upstream (commit) | License | Contents | Cases |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `force/` | [SolidLabResearch/ODRL-Test-Suite](https://github.com/SolidLabResearch/ODRL-Test-Suite) `7958238` — FORCE, Ghent/imec | MIT (`force/LICENSE.md`) | `data/{index.ttl, policies, requests, sotw, test_cases}`; expected Compliance Reports. `data/results` (their evaluator's run reports) omitted. | 68 |
| `oval/` | [DIPS-Tools/ODRL-Engine](https://github.com/DIPS-Tools/ODRL-Engine) `ee72ffc` — OVAL, Southampton | MIT (`oval/LICENSE`) | `access_control/` (policy, request JSON, expected decision with OVAL's semantics switches); `monitoring_compliant/`, `monitoring_non_compliant/` (policy, CSV event log, expected compliance; upstream's names since `81524b2`); `validation/valid_ODRL/`, `validation/invalid_ODRL/` (policies OVAL's SHACL validator must accept or reject, in Turtle and in JSON-LD with the W3C context by URL); `unit_tests.md` documents the switches, `evaluator_feature_support.md` the features. `force/` (their translation of FORCE) omitted. | 41 + 81, and 36 + 25 for validation |
| `w3c-fs/` | [w3c/odrl](https://github.com/w3c/odrl) `1db8e6b` `formal-semantics/examples/` — W3C ODRL CG | W3C Software and Document License (`w3c-fs/LICENSE.md`) | JSON-LD policies, evaluation requests, states, compliance reports. | 9 |

Refresh by re-cloning at a newer commit and re-running the translation; never edit files here.

Searched and not vendored: ODRL-PAP (tests are ODRL→Rego translations, not verdicts), odrl-manager (expectations embedded in TypeScript), ODRE (policies without expected verdicts), Gaia-X odrl-toolbox testbed (one case), W3C POE 2018 test material (structural validation only; superseded by `odrl22-shape.ttl`), DALICC (a license library without expected verdicts, contradicted by its own dependency graph), RDFLicense (license dump from before ODRL 2.2: every file fails both checkers, and no license is stated), the Mustafa et al. benchmark of arXiv:2602.19883 (conflict problems over pairs of constraints, in TPTP and SMT-LIB, not request verdicts; its ten runtime problems use left operands due2 does not bind). All three are annotated in `docs/design/references.md`.

## Triage of what was not translated

| Group | Count | Why | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| FORCE policies 1–7 (test cases 001–025) | 25 | Rules without `odrl:target` (and 1–2 without `odrl:action`). IM 2.6.1/2.6.2: a Permission and a Prohibition MUST have one target — these are not ODRL 2.2, and due2 rejects them at normalisation. They test FORCE's reading of an absent target as "any". | Translated as negative cases `force-01` … `force-07`: the expected answer is the rejection, and FORCE's results are kept. Reported upstream before — acknowledged, not fixed (2026-10-11); do not re-report. |
| OVAL `listRightOperand1–4` | 4 | `isPartOf` with a list right operand. Recorded until 2026-10-11 as a reading divergence; it was a due2 shape defect, now fixed (`odrl22-conformance.md` §2 erratum). At `f0839f6` the originals lacked an assigner (IM 2.1.2) and a target (IM 2.6.1); since `40b8ac6` they are targeted Sets. | Translated as `oval-list-right-operand`. |
| OVAL `date1` | 1 | Untargeted until `531edf1`; untyped right operand `"2020-03-11T11:33:10"`, request without time (OVAL substitutes the current time). | Translated as the negative case `oval-untyped-datetime` (2026-10-16). |
| OVAL `logic_with_nulls1–11`, `8b` | 12 | 1–9 added upstream in `596f10c` (2026-10-19); `8b` in `4d2db6a`, which also re-expected 8; 10 and 11 in `f6b7414`. Refinements on `odrl:print` with request values left out, flat and nested (`or`, `xone`, `and` inside `xone`), on permissions and on prohibitions. OVAL expects a decision with the missing values read as false, plus *conditional matches*: the values under which a rule would match. due2 answers `Indeterminate` and names the missing operands as unknown parts; `due2-xone-unknown`, `due2-nested-unknowns`, and `oval-no-target-prohibition` already cover those shapes. The conditional matches are an external answer to *what would change the decision*. | Investigated 2026-10-20, not translated. Deferred to #61, where the expected conditional matches can serve as vectors. |
| OVAL `validation/valid_ODRL/*`, `validation/invalid_ODRL/*` | 36 + 25 | Policies, no requests. `tools/check_odrl22.py` at `ee72ffc` rejects 9 of the 36 valid ones, some for more than one reason: 6 write `odrl:unit` as a string, which is what the W3C JSON-LD context produces (`"unit": "odrl:unit"`) though IM §2.5.1 makes the unit an IRI; 3 use terms neither the vocabulary nor a profile defines (`odrl12`: `runningTime`; `odrl13`: `ex:view`, `foaf:age`; `odrl24_edit1`: the action `acknowledge`); and `only_one_assigner_needed` and `only_one_assigner_assignee_needed` read IM §2.1.2–2.1.3 as one assigner per policy, where due2's shape requires one for every rule, at rule or policy level. It accepts 14 of the 25 invalid ones: a Rule nested under an edge outside its domain (a Prohibition under a Permission, a Remedy on a Duty, a Consequence on a Permission; 12 files), and an `odrl:refinement` on a Rule or Policy, where Vocabulary §3.14.3 restricts it to an Action or a collection (2). `tools/check_corpus.py` admits 13 of those 14, and two more that only the shape rejects (`odrl12_invalid`, `one_assigner_assignee_needed`). | Nesting and placement: the defect is due2's, #93. Unit and assigner: reading divergences, recorded here. |
| OVAL `monitoring_compliant/*`, `monitoring_non_compliant/*` | 81 | Compliance of an event log, not an access request. due2's monitoring question is open (workflows §9 #4). `logic_or`, `logic_xone`, `logic_nested*` are useful once it is specified. | Deferred to #4. |
| W3C CG A2 | — | Policy without evaluation requests. | Nothing to translate. |

## Findings

**For due2's specs** (registered where noted):

1. **Requests without a target** (OVAL `default_sem*`). OVAL accepts them and lets an evaluator switch decide (prohibit, permit, or unspecified by default). due2 decided (2026-10-11, workflows §3.2, §5.2, issue #26) that the target is optional and an absent one makes every relation part `U`, as an absent party already did: the verdict is `Indeterminate` when the target could decide it, and the default belongs to the enforcement point. Translated as `oval-no-target-permission`, `oval-no-target-prohibition`.
2. **`invalid` voids a policy** (OVAL `conflict3`). OVAL reports such a policy as not evaluable. due2 decided (2026-10-11, architecture §6.2) to keep *contributes nothing* (`NotApplicable`): validity is W1's and the checkers' concern, a self-voiding policy is an evaluation outcome visible in the trace, and OVAL's reading conflates the two. See `oval-conflict-invalid`.
3. **Refinement-free `odrl:source` on collections** (FORCE policies 16–18, 21). FORCE names collections by `odrl:source` and takes membership from `odrl:partOf` edges in the state of the world. Under due2's closure reading this is inert, so it is now admitted as an annotation (2026-10-11, `due2-profiles.md` §8.1) and the translations keep it. Collection refinements stay rejected (issue #21).
4. **Witness conditions as duty-action refinements** (OVAL duty1–3, CG C1–C2). Both write "pay at least/exactly x" as an `odrl:payAmount` refinement on `odrl:compensate`. Since 2026-10-11 `due2-core` binds `odrl:payAmount` to `due2:witnessSource` (`due2-profiles.md` §9 #6), so these policies need no binding of their own and are used as written.
5. **Conditional duties** (CG C2). A duty guarded by the request's weekday exposed two things. Under hoisting, independent completion widened the verdict to `Indeterminate`; workflows v0.6 fixed that with completions over literals. Hoisting itself was then withdrawn, because it is ×2^c for c guarded duties on one permission (`decisions/0003`). The CG's reading — duty Inactive, permission Active (C21) — is now due2's structure as well: guards stay on the duty.

**For the ODRL formal semantics** (WG material):

6. **Unfulfilled preconditions: three evaluators, three readings.** FORCE activates the permission ("given that eventually the duty is fulfilled"); OVAL parameterises it (`semantics_for_duties`, default accept); the CG examples deny (C11, C22). due2 answers `Pending` with the duty as the route — which is what all three approximate as yes/no.
7. **Unknown is false everywhere else.** FORCE ("if no information is present … not satisfied"), OVAL, and the CG examples all close unknowns to false. OVAL comes closest: it also reports *conditional matches*, rules that would match for some values of the request's unspecified features, with a warning — but its decision ignores them. At `40b8ac6`, inside a logical constraint the null re-evaluation was unreachable code, so an unspecified feature there was plain false (`ODRL_Evaluator.py` `eval_constraint`); `596f10c` made it reachable (see the upstream defects below). Until then none of the suites contained a case whose correct answer depends on an unknown. OVAL's `logic_with_nulls1–9` are the first, and they still expect the decision with the unknown read as false. `due2-or-unknown` and `w3c-fs-b1` scenario 3 are due2's own such cases.
8. **Absent default semantics is a policy-level choice in the CG** (`Behaviour`: default/close/open) and an evaluator switch in OVAL. due2 returns `NotApplicable` and leaves the default to the enforcement point.
9. **Comparison across XSD types.** CG A1/A2 compare an `xsd:dateTime` action time with `"2018-01-01"^^xsd:date`, and use timezone-less instants, which XSD orders only partially. ODRL 2.2 does not say how; due2 rejects the mismatch at normalisation.
10. **Refinement vs constraint failure.** CG B12 keeps a rule `Active` when its refinement fails (controlState Deny), while A12 makes it `Inactive` when its constraint fails. due2 treats both as the atom not applying.

**Upstream defects found while translating** (status per bullet):

- FORCE: policies 1–7 omit required targets; test case 036 is wired to `temporal-future.ttl` (duplicate of 038) though titled for the current time; `all-2023.ttl`/`all-2024.ttl` carry a DutyReport for policy-19's duty instead of policy-21's. Reported upstream once before (acknowledged, not fixed — 2026-10-11); re-reporting is pointless until they act.
- OVAL: a summary of the findings below was sent to the authors on 2026-10-11, with the offer to file issues. They acted on it within two days (`c2773ed` … `19692cc`, 2026-10-11 to 10-13): the test policies are Sets, every rule has a target, and their SHACL now requires targets and restricts `odrl:conflict` values and sub-rule types.
- OVAL: hierarchy reasoning (since 2026-08-27; unchanged at `ee72ffc`) covers only a rule's action, assignee and target. Constraint values get none: `isPartOf` and `hasPart` are plain subset tests, `isA` is unsupported, and a narrower SKOS purpose does not match `purpose eq` its broader one, so a prohibition fails open. Reported 2026-10-16 as [DIPS-Tools/ODRL-Engine#8](https://github.com/DIPS-Tools/ODRL-Engine/issues/8); due2's reading is issue #52.
- OVAL: null matching inside a logical constraint is unreachable (finding 7). Reported 2026-10-16 as [DIPS-Tools/ODRL-Engine#9](https://github.com/DIPS-Tools/ODRL-Engine/issues/9). Fixed upstream in `596f10c` (2026-10-19): constraints now evaluate to `True`, `False` or `None`, and a logical constraint reports the null conditions under which it would match. Three nested cases still fail there, reported on the issue the same day: the first, null-free pass still reads a missing value as false, so an `xone` with one true member and an unspecified one is accepted as a full match; and a member whose value is already decided still adds its null conditions, so `or(and(F, x), y)` reports `x or y` where only `y` helps. Our `due2-xone-unknown` scenario 1 is the first case in due2's terms. The suite was refreshed to `532db7c` on 2026-10-20, with the fix and its nine new tests. The two nested cases were fixed upstream the same day (`4d2db6a`), with `logic_with_nulls10` and `11` as their tests, and the suite was refreshed to `ee72ffc`. The remaining case, an `xone` with one true member and an unspecified one, is a semantics choice upstream: a missing value is false.
- OVAL: at `f0839f6`, 74 of its 105 policy files were Offers without an assigner (IM §2.1.2), rules were untargeted, and 85 of 105 failed ODRL 2.2 validation; both are fixed. At `40b8ac6`, 52 of 110 still fail, and at `532db7c` the same 52 of 119 (the nine `logic_with_nulls` files are valid): 47 use left operands that neither the ODRL vocabulary nor a declared profile defines (`ex:page`, `ex:age`, `ex:publicationDate`, and `odrl:adminLevel`, which is not an ODRL term; IM §2.1), and 5 write `odrl:unit` as a string literal (IM §2.5.1: an IRI). 17 write dateTime right operands untyped. At `ee72ffc`, 51 of the 122 access-control and monitoring policies fail: the same 47, 16 of which also use an action ODRL does not define (`odrl:create`, `ex:view`), and 4 units written as strings (`duty2` dropped its unit in `4362803`). Five monitoring policies (`monitoring_compliant/consequence1–2`, `monitoring_non_compliant/consequence3–5`) put `odrl:target` on the action node, where IM §2.6 places it on the Rule; neither checker detects it.
- W3C CG: C1/C2 requests name `party/billie1` against assignee `party/billie` while the expected reports permit; B11/B12 request values written `{"@id": "1000"}` with `describesFeature` the unit IRI rather than the operand; C12 `paymentDate` untyped.

## Traces compared (#60)

What each evaluator says beyond its decision, read 2026-10-17. Sources: FORCE's Compliance Report Model (`https://w3id.org/force/compliance-report#`) and the 68 expected reports in `force/data/test_cases/`; OVAL's `evaluate_ODRL_access_request_on_dataframe` at `40b8ac6` (read, never run); the W3C CG compliance reports in `w3c-fs/`. due2's side is workflows §3.5–§3.7 and `decisions/0010`–`0011`.

| Question | FORCE | OVAL (access control) | W3C CG examples | due2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Per rule | A `PermissionReport`, `ProhibitionReport` or `DutyReport`: `activationState` Active/Inactive, `attemptState`; for monitoring, `performanceState` and `deonticState` | The matched permissions and prohibitions, each with the rule's parsed form | A `ruleReport`: `activationState` Active/Inactive, `controlState` Permit/Deny | `finding` per atom and predicate, `T`/`F`/`U` |
| Per premise | `premiseReport`s for party, action, target and each constraint, with operands, operator, and `satisfactionState` Satisfied/Unsatisfied; nested for logical constraints | `conditions`: only the conditions that matched on an unspecified feature | `ConstraintReport` with `satisfactionState` Satisfied/Not-Satisfied | `basis`: the determining parts and their truth; fact values through `read` and the SOTW |
| Unknown | Not representable: "missing information" is Unsatisfied. `PerformanceState:Unknown` and `DeonticState:NonSet` are about monitoring, not data | A *conditional match*: listed with its null conditions and a warning, but the decision uses full matches only (finding 7) | Not representable | `U` survives to the verdict; `Indeterminate` names its pivotal `unknown` atoms and its `verdict_range` |
| Duties | `conditionReport` links a duty's report to its permission's; a Violated duty keeps the permission inactive | `duties`: the unfulfilled ones, per matched permission | A `ConditionReport` per duty, with an `ActionReport`: `performanceState`, `deonticState` (Fulfilled, Not-set) | `instance` per duty instance; `Pending` frontier with bearers; `obligation` and `closed` roles |
| Decision | None at policy level: rule reports only | accept, reject, or `None` | Per rule only | One of five verdicts, with `verdict_basis` |
| Conflict: remover and rule | Not modelled | An English sentence naming the strategy applied; the overridden rules are dropped from the lists, so the output no longer names them | Not modelled | `eliminated (atom | by_atom, rule)`, one tuple per remover |
| Composition | One policy and one request per report; `dct:created` only | One policy per call | One policy per report | Across policies by `policy_id` and the combination rule; across a case's evaluations by `seq` and a per-relation diff |
| Machine-readable | Yes (RDF) | Partly: lists of rules, explanations in English | Yes (JSON-LD) | Yes: typed relations under the canonical encoding (`decisions/0007`) |

**Can due2's trace be rendered as a compliance report?** For `T` and `F` findings, yes: an atom's `applies` maps to `activationState`, its basis parts to `premiseReport`s, its duty instances to `DutyReport`s. Three things are lost: `U` (no satisfaction state for it), the verdict, and `eliminated`. A third satisfaction state would remove the first loss. That is a possible friendly suggestion to the FORCE authors, parked until we have examples to show them (#62).

**Gaps in due2's trace.** None found. Everything the three record is in the trace or derivable from it with the inputs (§3.7). The question all three leave open, and due2 too, is *what would change the decision*. OVAL comes closest, with its conditional matches and its advice under `invalid` ("Either set a different conflict strategy…"). It is filed as #61 (remedies).

## Validator fixes the external data forced

- `tools/check_odrl22.py` ran with no inference, so an untyped rule (`odrl:permission [ … ]`, the IM's own example style) failed `sh:class odrl:Permission` **and** escaped `PermissionShape` — a missing target went unreported. It now adds the types the ODRL vocabulary entails (rdfs:range of the rule, action, target, and party properties; rdfs:domain of `odrl:leftOperand`; the connective of a Logical Constraint). The corpus still passes; external policies now fail for real reasons only.
- `tools/check_corpus.py` checked rejected constructs on policy, rule, and constraint nodes, never on asset or party nodes — where `odrl:source` and collection refinements actually occur (IM 2.5.5–2.5.6). It now checks them.
